findings.finding: The changes to client.ts, api.ts, and contracts.ts only remove export keywords; parsing at those boundaries is unchanged.
The rule options are config input; meta.defaultOptions lets oxlint merge them before schema validation, so the rule body reads a complete option.

Root cause: ModelConfig made compactThreshold optional for every model, so a Responses entry without it typechecked and sent compact_threshold: undefined. The compaction tests built exactly that config. The fix makes the field required by the union on wire. With the field optional again, the @ts-expect-error fixture fails the typecheck.

Root cause of the executeCommand removal: exports:check read only the TypeScript projects, so the import in tools/native-transport/server.mjs was invisible. The check now reads relative imports in tracked .js, .mjs, and .cjs files. With all 23 un-exported names exported again, it reports 22, so executeCommand was the only one with a JavaScript importer.
project/require-disable-reason accepted a disable comment for any named rule, so an inline disable could skip the reviewed allow list of project/no-type-assertion.
project/no-type-assertion read context.options[0].allow with no default, so enabling it as plain "error" crashed the plugin.
archive.ts, attempt.ts, session.ts, database.ts, jobs.ts, and worker.ts changed only by losing export keywords.
typecheck:range writes only into a fresh temporary directory, which it removes.
skills:record now rewrites a cited SHA to its in-range copy; running it twice over the same range writes the same record.

The earlier claim that no un-exported name had an importer was false: the measurement read only TypeScript, and tools/native-transport/server.mjs imports executeCommand. With the JavaScript scan, the other 22 names have no importer in tracked files here or on work/ui-pr3-d.
ResponsesModelKey and isResponsesModel had callers in providers.ts, responses.ts, and adapters.test.ts. All three now use the config narrowed on wire, and both names are deleted.
range-typecheck.cjs and exports-check.cjs sit beside audit-check.cjs and security-check.cjs, and each has one npm script and one checks.cjs entry.
